_note: THE HOTEL ADMIN CAPABILITY CONTRACT. Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at BUILD time: a variable that is absent when `next build` runs is not merely empty, it is never substituted, and the compiled comparison `"1" === process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE2_ADMIN` is evaluated in the browser against an empty env shim and is therefore ALWAYS FALSE. The routes still compile and remain reachable by URL, so nothing crashes and nothing 404s - the operator simply loses the navigation to them. That is exactly how a bundle built with no flags was deployed to the PRE-LIVE appliance and served an operator surface with no Internet Packages, no Service Plans and no PMS Connection while every structural check passed. This file is what a build is held to, so that outcome cannot be produced silently again.
applies_to: PRE-LIVE appliance and every later Hotel Admin release until the contract is deliberately changed

required_build_flags._note: Every flag MUST be present in the build environment with exactly this value. Packaging supplies them from this file and then PROVES the substitution happened, because supplying a variable and having it inlined are two different facts.

required_routes._note: Operator surfaces that must exist in the built app-path route manifest. A build that cannot serve these is not a candidate for this appliance, whatever else is right about it.

required_navigation._note: The gated NAVIGATION, which is the thing the operator actually sees and the thing that silently disappeared. Each entry names a capability flag and one route it must lead to; verification asserts the compiled bundle can reach the route AND that the flag governing it was inlined true.

forbidden_in_client_bundle._note: A residual runtime lookup of a capability flag in the CLIENT chunks is the fingerprint of a build that never received it: Next left the property access in place instead of substituting a literal. Finding one of these means the flag was missing however confidently the build environment was set up, so it is a hard packaging failure rather than a warning.

minimum_rollback_contract._note: A rollback target must be able to operate this appliance. A release that predates these surfaces would remove PMS, Service Plan and Package management from the operator the moment it was served, so it is archive evidence and NOT an executable rollback, however recently it was deployed.
